Shows and records observed LTE/5G bands for each SIM. For supported Japanese carriers, it compares observed bands with reference bands. It does not measure signal strength or real network quality.

• Checks about every 1.5 seconds on screen or every 3 seconds in background.
🟦 Dark: Connected now
⬜ Light: Observed
⬛ Gray: Reference band not yet observed
Observed data and statistics are kept separately for each SIM. You can share reports or export per-SIM CSV logs.

Tap the percentage to view SIM-specific observed bands and statistics. This is the share of reference bands seen so far, not signal quality or all bands supported by the phone.

Q. Does background monitoring affect battery life?
A. Monitoring periodically reads mobile network information, approximately every 3 seconds in the background. Battery consumption depends on the device and OS.
Q. How frequently are bands checked?
A. Approximately every 1.5 seconds on the main screen and every 3 seconds while background monitoring runs. Android may supply cached or incomplete cell information.
Q. Does it work with overseas carriers?
A. It can show the carrier name and bands provided by Android. Without registered reference bands, the compatibility percentage is N/A. Availability varies by device.
Q. Why are some connected bands not showing up?
A. On certain smartphones, OS or manufacturer restrictions prevent the currently connected band information from being shared with apps.
Q. Can I use physical SIM and eSIM together?

A. Active SIMs are shown in separate tabs, including supported configurations with three or more active subscriptions. If Android cannot identify a band for a particular SIM, the app does not assign it to another SIM.
Q. What is the difference between N/A and 0%?
A. N/A means there is no carrier reference or insufficient observations. 0% means observations exist but none match the reference bands.
Q. Does 23% mean my phone has poor signal or supports only 23% of bands?
A. No. This is the share of registered carrier reference bands observed so far, not radio signal strength, coverage quality, or a full list of phone-supported bands.
